subject: Capacity top-up, fee structure adjustment & SOW line-item edits
messages:
From: Maggie Chen <maggie.chen@sunrisehealth.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2025-04-18T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Capacity increase request + SOW edits

Sergio —

Thanks again for the walkthrough this morning. We need to accelerate our Q3 capacity planning: internal forecasts show an additional ~6x A100-equivalent nodes for our private deployment (approx 30% uplift) starting July 1. Procurement is asking for:

- A short change order that increases committed capacity (exhibit A line items) OR a clearly priced burst + reserved approach
- A revised fee schedule showing per-node month pricing and any one-time provisioning charges
- Explicit SOW language for acceptance tests and cutover windows (we cannot exceed 7-day outage windows during our migration)

Can you send a redline and commercial summary by end of week? Our legal and procurement teams (procurement@sunrisehealth.com) will review but want to see Redwood's proposed wording first.

Also flag: we may request a short pilot (60 days) on the new nodes before fully committing to the larger top-up.

Appreciate it —
Maggie Chen
Director, Cloud Procurement
Sunrise Health

Attachments: internal forecast (referenced in body)
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maggie Chen <maggie.chen@sunrisehealth.com>
Cc: procurement@sunrisehealth.com
Date: 2025-04-18T09:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity increase request + SOW edits

Maggie —

Thanks, got it. Summary of what we’ll provide by Friday EOD:

1) Draft change order (redlined against current Order Form + Exhibit A) that:
   - Adds 6 A100-equivalent nodes (private) starting 2025-07-01
   - Shows tiered per-node pricing (reserved vs burst) and a one-time provisioning fee
2) Clean, commercial summary (one-pager) with three options: (A) Reserved commitment (best unit price), (B) Burst pool + reserved base, (C) Pilot 60-day trial for 6 nodes with monthly opt-in
3) SOW edits to Exhibit A for acceptance criteria and migration windows (we'll propose phased acceptance tests to limit outage risk)

Ballpark (high level) — subject to legal/commercial sign-off: $12,000 / node / month reserved; burst = $15,500 / node / month; provisioning fee = $8,000 (one-time). I will surface the precise numbers in the commercial summary.

Looping in Laura Bennett (legal) and Karthik Iyer (solutions) to review redlines and confirm SLA/acceptance language. Laura — could you please focus on: liability caps for cutover-related incidents, SLA migration carve-outs, and acceptance test phrasing? Also flag any procurement asks that would require exec approval.

Next steps: internal review -> send redline back to you with comment summary -> procurement/legal review -> target signature/DocuSign in mid-May if timelines hold.

Thanks —
Sergio Alvarez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2025-04-21T16:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Capacity increase request + SOW edits — legal review needed

Sergio & Karthik —

Quick legal review notes after a pass of the attached PDF redline (Sunrise_CO_20250418_redline.pdf):

1) Fees / Billing
   - Add explicit language in Order Form Section 4.2: "One-time provisioning fees are invoiced upon execution and are non-refundable."
   - Clarify invoicing schedule for the pilot: "Customer will be invoiced monthly in arrears for pilot usage; reserved capacity invoices will begin upon pilot conversion to full commitment."

2) Acceptance & Cutover
   - Replace single global acceptance with phased acceptance (Exhibit A): provide 3 checkpoints (provisioning verification, baseline latency/throughput test, final cutover)
   - Add a carve-out: "Incidents during accepted maintenance windows will not constitute SLA violations; maintenance windows shall not exceed seven (7) consecutive days without mutual written agreement."

3) Liability / Remedies
   - Preserve existing MSA liability cap but add narrowly tailored carve-out language for gross negligence. Do NOT broaden customer termination rights for provisioning delays under 30 days.

4) Data & Audit Requests
   - For procurement audit requests, add: "Customer audit requests will be limited to one on-site or virtual audit per 12-month period and will be subject to reasonable notice and confidentiality protections."

5) Minor drafting items
   - Cross-reference clean-up between Order Form Exhibit A and Section 2.1 (Service Descriptions). Avoid duplicative acceptance criteria.

I've annotated the PDF with line-level comments. Commercial to confirm the exact numbers for the provisioning fee and pilot invoicing schedule before we send to Sunrise. Once numbers are confirmed, I can prepare a short legal cover note for the change order and a finalized redline for DocuSign.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
